references.text: Moses chooses leaders over the tribes and appoints them as commanders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, just as in Exodus 18:25.
Mentions commanders over thousands and commanders over hundreds, the same hierarchical structure that Moses established.
Refers to the commanders of the army divisions, the thousand-leaders and hundred-leaders, the same leadership structure.
The thousand-leaders and hundred-leaders are mentioned in connection with war spoils, showing the military organizational structure.
Judges and officials shall be appointed in all cities, a continuation of the legal system Moses established.
Samuel warns that the king will appoint commanders over thousands and over fifties, the same division.
Saul refers to commanders over thousands and over hundreds, showing the continuation of the leadership structure.
David organizes the army with commanders over thousands and over hundreds, the same system Moses introduced.
David consults with the commanders over thousands and hundreds, still using Moses' organizational structure.
Describes Israel's organization with commanders over thousands and hundreds who served the king.
The commanders over thousands and hundreds in Israel are mentioned among those who gave voluntary gifts to the temple.
The apostles choose men full of the Spirit and wisdom to serve, a similar principle for selecting leaders as in Exodus 18.
Confirms that Moses' organizational model became a lasting institutional standard for Israel's army in later times.
